title: Electric Circuits
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Electric Circuits Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the parts of a circuit; distinguish conductors and insulators; build and compare series and parallel circuits; describe how electricity is generated and ways to use it safely and conserve it. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Electrical Phenomena)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets on circuits, conductors and insulators, series and parallel circuits, electrical safety and saving electricity in Ontario. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Current flows in a closed circuit.
key_sub: Series circuits have one path; parallel circuits have many, so one bulb can go out alone.
body_html:
How to think about it

A circuit needs an energy source, conductors and a closed loop.

  • Conductors (metals) let current flow; insulators (plastic, rubber, wood) do not.
  • Series circuit: one path. Parallel circuit: several paths, like wiring in a house.
  • Generators in power plants change motion into electricity; we pay for energy in kWh.
  • Safety: keep water away, do not overload outlets, stay away from power lines.
Example

A switch is open. Does the bulb light?

there is a gap

Answer: no

Example

One bulb in a parallel circuit breaks. Do the others stay on?

other paths are complete

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a battery 'pushes out' only one way so the second wire is not needed.
  • Mixing up series and parallel.
  • Thinking all metals are insulators when they are cold.

faq.q: What is the difference between a series and a parallel circuit?
faq.a: A series circuit has one path. A parallel circuit has two or more paths, so devices work on their own.

faq.q: Why are wires covered in plastic?
faq.a: Plastic is an insulator, so it keeps the current in the wire and protects people from shocks.

Circuit A has 1 battery and 2 bulbs in parallel. Circuit B has 2 batteries and 3 bulbs in series. All the batteries and bulbs are the same. In which circuit is each bulb brighter?
items.e: More batteries in series make bulbs brighter. Bulbs in series share and are dimmer; each bulb in parallel is as bright as one bulb alone.
